rules.rule: Check for urgent weakness or tiredness conditions
rules.problem: Type, trigger (Fatigue or Asthenia) and contents match the red box, except that nothing captures 'Hb < 6' (red-box item p43-59e753c2). No g/dL unit exists in the grammar, so a measurement is not possible; a finding such as (snomed_concept "Hemoglobin below reference range" "finding") (confirmed with exists) could stand in, or the gap should be recorded in remaining questions.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible stroke (weakness or tiredness page)
rules.problem: 'consider stroke' -> possible is right; (and trigger (or signs)) matches the page. Only the missing Sudden onset on difficulty speaking / visual disturbance (claim level).

rules.rule: Diagnose possible TIA (weakness or tiredness page)
rules.problem: 'consider ... TIA' -> possible is right; same structure note as stroke.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable heart failure (weakness or tiredness page)
rules.problem: 'heart failure likely' -> probable; page says 'worse on lying flat AND leg swelling', rule uses and. Faithful.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable dehydration (weakness or tiredness page)
rules.problem: The page lists 'Thirst, dry mouth, poor skin turgor, BP < 90/60, dehydration likely' as one cluster of signs (contrast the heart-failure line, which spells out 'and'). The rule ORs all five, so tiredness plus dry mouth alone yields probable dehydration, which then fires Urgent and the ORS/IV pathway. The page's intent is ambiguous but the or reading is the loosest possible; any2 (as the gold page uses for clustered signs) or a note in remaining questions is warranted.

rules.rule: Urgent: weakness or tiredness with red-box findings
rules.problem: Urgent level and (and complaint (or ...)) shape are right, but the red-box item 'Hb < 6' (p43-59e753c2) is missing entirely, so a patient with tiredness and Hb < 6 is never escalated. The grammar has no g/dL unit; use a finding (e.g. (snomed_concept "Hemoglobin below reference range" "finding")) or document the gap. Also: (active_condition Fever) drops the 3-day window (low), and Sudden onset is missing on difficulty talking / visual disturbance (medium).

rules.rule: (missing) Diagnose probable anaemia (weakness or tiredness page)
rules.problem: Outside the red box the page says 'Check Hb. If < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man), anaemia likely' (p43-9b35877c). The brief asks for every 'X likely' as a probable diagnosis; none is written. (snomed_concept "Anemia" "disorder") exists. If Hb cannot be expressed as a measurement, record it in remaining questions.

summary: The red-box item 'Hb < 6' is not encoded anywhere, so the Urgent priority rule misses one of the ten red-box criteria; the out-of-box 'anaemia likely' (Hb < 12 woman / < 13 man) also has no probable rule. The dehydration rule ORs five signs the page presents as a cluster, so a single sign (e.g. dry mouth) with tiredness yields probable dehydration and an Urgent escalation. Difficulty speaking and visual disturbance lack the Sudden onset qualifier that the stroke/TIA line implies, and (active_condition Fever) drops the 3-day window; all other claims are faithful and every SNOMED concept resolves.
